meta.name: The Best Dog Parks in San Francisco & the Peninsula
meta.title_tag: Best Dog Parks in San Francisco & Peninsula
meta.excerpt: From the off-leash cliffs of Fort Funston to fully fenced turf parks in Pacific Heights and Foster City, these are the highest-rated dog parks in San Francisco and the Peninsula — with fencing, hours, surfaces, and the leash rules that actually matter, each checked against its official city or park-district page in July 2026.
meta.meta_description: Top-rated dog parks in San Francisco and down the Peninsula to Redwood City: off-leash areas, fencing, hours and rules. Verified July 2026.

hero.alt: Fort Funston — from Wooffy's Bay Area dog guide (photo: Tim Adams, CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons)

body_html:
San Francisco and the Peninsula are packed with places to let a dog stretch its legs, from wind-scoured coastal bluffs to tidy fenced turf runs. This guide covers the best dog parks in San Francisco and down the Peninsula to Redwood City, with the practical details owners actually need — whether it is fenced, whether dogs can go off-leash, the surface underfoot, shade, water, and parking. Every rule below was verified July 2026 against the park's official National Park Service, city, or park-district page.

Alongside the official rules, we distilled recurring themes from dog-owner reviews across Google, Yelp, Reddit, BringFido, and AllTrails — see the “What dog owners say” notes under each entry (a theme is included only when it shows up on at least two independent platforms).

Here is how we chose these. We started from every dog park in San Francisco and the Peninsula, as far south as Redwood City, that has at least 100 Google reviews, then kept only the ones rated 4.3 stars or higher. We ranked those by rating and then by number of reviews, and confirmed each park's dog rules against its official National Park Service, city, or park-district page. The parks appear below in that ranked order.

Fort Funston (San Francisco)

Address: Skyline Blvd near John Muir Dr, San Francisco, CA 94132 · Off-leash: yes — voice-and-sight control in designated areas · Fenced: no · Hours: sunrise to sunset · Cost: free (free parking lot off Skyline Blvd)

★ 4.8 · 4,056 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo
SizeAbout two miles of beach below the bluffs
SurfaceSand and dune trails; one paved loop up top
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeNone — open and exposed
WaterDog-rinse spigot near the lot; bring your own to drink
ParkingFree lot off Skyline Blvd

Fort Funston is the marquee off-leash spot in the Bay Area: 200-foot sandstone bluffs above roughly two miles of beach, run by the National Park Service as part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area. Dogs range off-leash under voice and sight control across much of the headland and the southern beach, so regulars come at dawn before the wind and crowds build. There is no fence and the cliff edges are real, so this is a place for dogs with dependable recall, not escape artists.

Two things to plan for. The trail back up from the beach is a steep, sandy haul that punishes senior dogs, puppies, and out-of-shape humans. And the northern end by the bank swallow habitat goes leash-only or dog-free to protect nesting birds from roughly spring through summer, so read the posted signs before you unclip. It is often cold, windy, and foggy when the rest of the city is sunny, and the Skyline lot fills by mid-morning on sunny weekends.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 vast off-leash dunes, trails, and beach feel like a giant dog playground
  • 👍 dogs and owners are unusually friendly and well-socialized — great for shy dogs to make friends
  • 👍 dramatic ocean views with hang gliders overhead make the walk fun for humans too
  • ⚠️ the climb back up from the beach is steep and sandy — hard on seniors, puppies, and out-of-shape humans
  • ⚠️ frequently cold, windy, and foggy even when the rest of the city is sunny
  • ⚠️ weekends get jammed with dogs and the parking lot fills quickly

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, AllTrails.

Crissy Field (San Francisco)

Address: 1199 East Beach, Presidio, San Francisco, CA 94129 · Off-leash: areas — voice control at Central Beach and part of the airfield · Fenced: no · Hours: dawn to dusk · Cost: free (paid/metered parking lots)

★ 4.7 · 6,137 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo
SizeWide beach plus former airfield
SurfaceSand beach, grass airfield, paved promenade
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeLittle
WaterDog-wash station and water fountain
ParkingPaid or metered lots

Crissy Field pairs a flat, wide beach with a grassy former airfield and a bayfront promenade under the Golden Gate Bridge. Under GGNRA rules, dogs may go off-leash under voice and sight control at the Central Crissy Field beach and on about a third of the adjacent airfield; the picnic lawns and parking areas are on-leash only. The dog crowd on the beach is playful, and owners tend to pay attention.

The seasonal rules trip up first-timers. West Beach is dog-free to protect the endangered western snowy plover, a plover protection zone near the beach is on-leash from July 1 through May 15, and the Crissy Marsh and fenced vegetation areas are off-limits year-round. A dog-wash station and water fountain make the muddy-paw cleanup easy. Come early, because the lots and metered spaces go fast and the fog and wind arrive without much warning.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 off-leash beach time with a Golden Gate Bridge backdrop is hard to beat
  • 👍 friendly, playful dog crowd on East Beach with owners who pay attention
  • 👍 flat promenade, grass, and a dog wash station/water fountain make cleanup and cool-down easy
  • ⚠️ seasonal snowy-plover leash restrictions on the western beach (July through mid-May) catch first-timers off guard — you have to read the signs
  • ⚠️ completely unfenced and near parking lots and busy paths, so dogs need reliable recall

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, DogTrekker.

Seal Point Park Dog Park (San Mateo)

Address: 1801 E 3rd Ave, San Mateo, CA 94401 (Seal Point Park, 1901 J. Hart Clinton Dr) · Off-leash: yes — fenced dog park · Fenced: yes · Hours: park hours, dawn to dusk · Cost: free

★ 4.7 · 1,706 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double-gated
Size3 acres
SurfaceCrushed gravel over dirt; dusty when dry
Small-dog areaYes, separate run
ShadeShaded bench seating
WaterDog and human fountains, plus bowls
ParkingFree lot

Seal Point is a three-acre fenced dog park on a breezy, reclaimed-landfill bayfront park, with double-gated entrances and a genuinely separate small-dog run so toy breeds and puppies are not swept up with the sprinters. The ground is crushed gravel over dirt, which holds mud down but kicks up dust in dry spells. Water bowls, human and dog fountains, shaded benches, and stocked waste-bag stations round it out, and San Mateo caps handlers at three dogs each.

Sitting right on the bay, it runs windier and cooler than inland parks, so bring a jacket for yourself and a coat for a thin-skinned dog. A free lot and direct access to the Bay Trail make it easy to tack on an on-leash loop before or after park time.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 huge 3-acre fenced run — one of the biggest on the Peninsula — with genuinely separate big and small dog areas
  • 👍 well-kept amenities: restrooms, human and dog drinking fountains, shaded seating, and stocked poop bags
  • 👍 direct access to the Bay Trail for an on-leash walk before or after park time
  • ⚠️ reliably windy coming off the bay — regulars warn newcomers to expect it
  • ⚠️ the crushed-gravel/dirt surface kicks up dust in dry months

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, DogPack.

Dog Park | Pine Lake Park (San Francisco)

Address: Sloat Blvd and Vale St, San Francisco, CA 94116 · Off-leash: yes — unfenced · Fenced: no · Hours: 5 a.m. to midnight · Cost: free (free street parking)

★ 4.7 · 586 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo
SizeOpen grassy meadow
SurfaceGrass; soft and muddy in winter
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeYes — tall eucalyptus
WaterNot listed
ParkingFree street parking on Vale and Wawona

At the west end of Sigmund Stern Grove, Pine Lake's off-leash area is a grassy meadow beside the lake, shaded by tall eucalyptus and calmer than the city's fenced turf pens. It is a place for dogs that want to open up and run rather than circle a small enclosure, and the tree cover is a rare bit of shade among the city's dog parks.

It is unfenced, with the lake and a walking path close by, so a reliable recall matters. The grass goes soft and muddy through the winter rains, so pack a towel in the wet months. Street parking along Vale and Wawona is usually easy outside peak weekend hours.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Big open grassy meadow where large and small dogs can really sprint off-leash
  • 👍 Mature eucalyptus shade and the adjacent lake keep it cool on rare hot days
  • 👍 Peaceful natural setting beside Stern Grove that regulars pair with long walks
  • ⚠️ Turns soggy and muddy in wet or foggy weather
  • ⚠️ Off-leash section isn't fully fenced, so it suits dogs with reliable recall

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Rover, SF Rec & Park.

Lafayette Park Dog Play Area (San Francisco)

Address: Washington and Laguna St, San Francisco, CA 94115 · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes (fully enclosed, double-gated) · Hours: 5 a.m. to midnight · Cost: free (street parking only)

★ 4.7 · 439 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, fully enclosed and double-gated
SizeCompact single pen
SurfaceK9 artificial turf; drains well
Small-dog areaNo separate section
ShadeLittle natural shade
WaterNot listed
ParkingStreet only, some grades steep

Renovated in 2019, Lafayette Park's pen is one of the cleanest in the city: a fully enclosed, double-gated run laid with premium artificial turf and a drainage system that keeps it usable in wet weather, when grass parks turn to soup. It perches in Pacific Heights with peeks of the Bay, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate Bridge.

It is a single compact yard with little natural shade, so it gets busy after work and on weekend mornings, and there is no separate small-dog section. Even so, the secure gating and even turf make it a strong choice for small or easily startled dogs. Plan on street parking in the surrounding neighborhood, some of it on a noticeable grade.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 2019-renovated K9 artificial turf drains well and stays clean and usable even in wet weather
  • 👍 Fully enclosed, double-gated run makes off-leash play feel secure
  • 👍 Postcard Pacific Heights views of the Bay, Golden Gate, and Alcatraz
  • ⚠️ Sits on a steep slope beside busy streets; parking on the grade unnerves some owners
  • ⚠️ The enclosed turf run is on the small side and open at the entrance rather than fully sealed

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, SF Rec & Park, Wag!.

Upper Douglass Dog Play Area (San Francisco)

Address: 26th and Douglass St, San Francisco, CA 94114 · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes · Hours: 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., closed Wednesdays · Cost: free (street parking)

★ 4.7 · 415 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes
SizeSpacious by city standards
SurfaceFlat grass field plus woodsy dirt trails
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeYes — mature trees and shaded seating
WaterNot listed
ParkingStreet only; short climb from most spots

On a Noe Valley hillside above the ballfield, Upper Douglass is a fenced off-leash area with a flat grassy field plus woodsy dirt trails winding up the slope. It is one of the few fenced SF dog parks with real grass instead of turf, which many dogs prefer underfoot, and the long sight lines and mature trees suit a relaxed, tight-knit regular crowd.

Long-standing drainage problems mean the grass and hillside turn muddy in the rain, and the field closes every Wednesday for maintenance and often through the wet winter months to let the grass recover, which frustrates regulars. Access is by street parking along Douglass, with a short climb up from most spots.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Fully fenced with varied terrain: a flat grassy field plus woodsy hillside dirt trails to explore
  • 👍 Mature trees, long sight lines, and shaded seating with a relaxed, tight-knit regular crowd
  • 👍 Well-maintained and spacious by city standards
  • ⚠️ Grass and hillside get muddy in the rain due to long-standing drainage problems
  • ⚠️ Closed every Wednesday and often through the wet winter months for field recovery, which frustrates regulars

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, SF Rec & Park, SF Examiner.

Foster City Dog Park (Foster City)

Address: 1001 Bounty Dr (Bounty Blvd at Foster City Blvd), Foster City, CA 94404 · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes (separate small and large sections) · Hours: daily, dawn to 10 p.m. · Cost: free (free lot)

★ 4.5 · 569 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes
SizeTwo separate runs
SurfaceSynthetic turf and decomposed granite
Small-dog areaYes, separate run
ShadeYes
WaterWatering stations throughout
ParkingFree lot at 1001 Bounty Dr

Foster City's dog park has two fenced runs, one for large dogs and one for small, laid with a mix of synthetic turf and decomposed granite, with watering stations, shade, seating, and bag dispensers throughout. It is flat, drains well, and holds up year-round, and the separate small-dog pen genuinely helps under-25-pound or timid dogs.

Two things regulars flag: the heavily used turf can be rough on sensitive paws, and there are recurring reports of distracted owners and the occasional aggressive-dog scuffle, so keep an eye on play rather than your phone. It fills up on weekend afternoons. The free lot right at 1001 Bounty Drive keeps access simple.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Separate large- and small-dog areas keep play size-appropriate
  • 👍 Artificial turf stays clean and mud-free even after rain
  • 👍 Shade, water fountains, and seating, with a friendly community of responsible regulars
  • ⚠️ Recurring aggressive-dog incidents and distracted owners on their phones, leading to preventable fights
  • ⚠️ Gets crowded on weekend afternoons
  • ⚠️ Heavily used turf can be rough on sensitive paws

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Tripadvisor, City of Foster City.

Centennial Dog Park (South San Francisco)

Address: Antoinette Lane and Chestnut Ave, South San Francisco, CA 94080 (along the Centennial Way Trail) · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes (airlock gates, separate small and large areas) · Hours: dawn to dusk · Cost: free

★ 4.5 · 481 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, double airlock gates
SizeLarge, two runs
SurfaceTurf plus packed dirt and cedar shavings
Small-dog areaYes, separate run
ShadeLimited; some shaded seating small-dog side
WaterFountains on both sides
ParkingTrail corridor and nearby streets

Set along the Centennial Way Trail on a former BART right-of-way, this park is securely fenced with double airlock gates and split into separate large- and small-dog runs. A surface of turf plus packed dirt and cedar shavings keeps it clean and mud-free year-round, both sides have water fountains, and the small-dog area has some shaded seating. A community bulletin board posts etiquette and obedience classes.

One practical tip: the entrance nearest the Safeway is often locked, which can mean a walk around to the far gate. Shade is otherwise limited and the site can feel exposed. Running right alongside the trail, it pairs naturally with a longer walk or bike ride; park along the trail corridor or nearby streets by Orange Memorial Park.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Large layout with separate runs for big and small dogs and plenty of room to run
  • 👍 Stays clean and mud-free year-round thanks to turf plus packed dirt and cedar shavings
  • 👍 Water, waste stations, benches, and a community bulletin board with etiquette and obedience classes
  • ⚠️ The entrance near Safeway is often locked, forcing a walk to the far gate
  • ⚠️ Limited shade and can feel exposed

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Foursquare, City of South San Francisco.

Treasure Island Dog Park (San Francisco)

Address: Avenue of Palms and 9th St, Treasure Island, San Francisco, CA 94130 · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes (fully fenced, multiple gates) · Hours: dawn to dusk · Cost: free (free parking)

★ 4.5 · 452 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes, fully fenced with multiple gates
SizeBig open field
SurfaceGrass; bumpy and uneven, with dig holes
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeAlmost none
WaterNot listed
ParkingFree parking

This fully fenced, grassy park sits right on the bay with wide-open views of the San Francisco skyline, the Bay Bridge, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate. There is plenty of room to run and several gates — double-check each one is latched behind you. The ground is bumpy and uneven, pocked with potholes where dogs have dug.

The setting is exposed: cold bay wind, almost no shade, and minimal seating (about one picnic table), so bring a layer and your own water. It sits next to a playground but has its own gated entrance, and afterward leashed dogs are welcome on the patio at the nearby Mersea restaurant, which makes for an easy morning out on the island.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 Jaw-dropping panoramic views of the Bay, Golden Gate, Bay Bridge, Alcatraz, and the skyline
  • 👍 Big open, fully fenced grassy field with multiple gates and lots of room to run
  • 👍 Quiet, low-key spot to relax while the dog plays
  • ⚠️ Very exposed to cold bay wind
  • ⚠️ Almost no shade and minimal seating (roughly one picnic table)
  • ⚠️ Bumpy, uneven ground with potholes from dogs digging

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, BringFido, Google Maps.

Bayside Dog Exercise Park (Burlingame)

Address: 1125 Airport Blvd, Burlingame, CA 94010 · Off-leash: yes — fenced · Fenced: yes (separate small and large areas) · Hours: 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. (closed Thursdays 7–9 a.m. for maintenance) · Cost: free (free lot)

★ 4.4 · 145 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedYes
SizeThree-quarter acre
SurfaceDecomposed granite and dirt, no grass
Small-dog areaYes, separate section
ShadeMinimal — a small pergola
WaterWater station on site
ParkingFree lot at 1125 Airport Blvd

Bayside is a three-quarter-acre fenced exercise park by the bay, divided into separate large- and small-dog areas, with a long, narrow big-dog run that is well suited to full-speed fetch. The surface is decomposed granite and dirt rather than grass — dusty in summer — with a water station and a small pergola for limited shade. Burlingame allows two dogs per handler and requires dogs to be over four months old, licensed, and vaccinated.

The most repeated gripe is odor drifting from the adjacent wastewater treatment plant, and with little shade it is best on cooler days. The free lot at 1125 Airport Boulevard makes it a handy stop near SFO. Fill any holes your dog digs, as posted, and note the Thursday 7–9 a.m. maintenance closure.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 long, narrow big-dog run that's great for full-speed fetch
  • 👍 separate small-dog section plus a water station for dogs
  • 👍 a caring group of regulars who look after the seating area and keep the vibe welcoming
  • ⚠️ odor from the adjacent wastewater treatment plant is the most repeated gripe
  • ⚠️ all-dirt surface with no grass — dusty in summer — and very limited shade

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, DogPack.

Corona Heights Dog Run (San Francisco)

Address: Roosevelt Way at Museum Way, San Francisco, CA 94117 · Off-leash: yes — unfenced · Fenced: no · Hours: 5 a.m. to midnight · Cost: free (Randall Museum lot and street parking)

★ 4.7 · 210 Google reviews · on Google Maps

FencedNo
SizeHillside run
SurfaceDirt and rock, with exposed bedrock
Small-dog areaNo
ShadeLittle — exposed hilltop
WaterNot listed (restrooms on site)
ParkingRandall Museum lot and street parking

Corona Heights is a rustic, unfenced off-leash run at the base of the 520-foot Corona Heights peak, next to the Randall Museum. The dirt-and-rock ground, exposed bedrock, and big city views give it a wild, hilltop feel more like a hike than a manicured dog park, and the varied terrain gives energetic dogs a real workout.

With no fence and a steep hill just above, this is a spot for dogs with solid recall rather than escape artists, and the exposed summit gets seriously windy — bring layers. Restrooms are on site. Park at the Randall Museum lot, with more street parking around the base of the hill.

Official page

What dog owners say:

  • 👍 panoramic city views from the summit — one of the most scenic dog outings in SF
  • 👍 fenced, double-gated wood-chip run plus adjoining off-leash hillside trails in one visit
  • 👍 rocky, varied terrain gives energetic dogs a genuine workout
  • ⚠️ the exposed hilltop gets seriously windy — bring layers
  • ⚠️ the fenced run itself is small, wood-chip only, with no big/small separation
  • ⚠️ steep paths and scarce street parking near the entrances

Recurring themes from owner reviews across Yelp, TripAdvisor, BringFido, DogPack.

Know Before You Go

  • Off your own property, dogs must be leashed everywhere except inside a designated off-leash area. In San Francisco the leash limit is eight feet; San Mateo County and its cities have similar leash-in-parks rules.
  • The off-leash zones at Fort Funston and Crissy Field are National Park Service voice-and-sight-control areas — your dog must respond to voice and hand commands and stay out of the posted leash-only and wildlife zones, and the snowy plover and bank swallow closures shift by season.
  • Dogs over four months old must have a current license and rabies vaccination under San Francisco Health Code, and county rules are comparable. Carry proof if asked.
  • Handler limits vary by jurisdiction: San Francisco dog play areas allow up to eight dogs per walker, San Mateo caps three dogs per handler, and Burlingame's Bayside park allows two per owner.
  • Always carry poop bags and pick up immediately. Several parks, including Bayside, also post a rule to fill any holes your dog digs.
  • At fenced parks with double or airlock gates (Seal Point, Lafayette, Foster City, Centennial, Bayside, Treasure Island), leash up before entering and exiting and latch every gate behind you.
  • For small or shy dogs, use the separate small-dog areas at Seal Point, Foster City, Centennial, and Bayside.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which of these dog parks are fully fenced?

Lafayette Park, Upper Douglass, Foster City, Centennial, Treasure Island, Bayside, and Seal Point are fenced off-leash parks. Fort Funston, Crissy Field, Pine Lake, and Corona Heights are open, unfenced off-leash areas, so bring a dog with reliable recall.

Where can my dog run off-leash on the beach?

Fort Funston and the Central Crissy Field beach both allow off-leash play under voice and sight control, per Golden Gate National Recreation Area rules. Watch for seasonal leash zones and closures that protect nesting snowy plovers and bank swallows, and check the posted signs before letting your dog loose.

Are these dog parks free?

Yes, all of them are free to enter. Most have free parking lots or street parking. The main exception is Crissy Field, where the beach and airfield are free but the parking lots are paid or metered.

Which is best for a small or timid dog?

Seal Point, Foster City, Centennial, and Bayside all have separate fenced small-dog sections. Lafayette Park's clean, enclosed turf pen is also a good choice for little dogs that would get lost in a big open field.

Do I need a license for my dog?

Yes. In San Francisco and across San Mateo County, dogs over four months old must be licensed and current on their rabies vaccination. Licensing helps reunite lost dogs with owners, and you should be prepared to show proof of vaccination if asked.
